dbl-invtrig: glibc 2.39 asin/acos (e_asin.c), atan (s_atan.c), atan2 (e_atan2.c)
Reproduces: Ubuntu 2.39-0ubuntu8.x x86-64 libm.so.6 on an FMA+AVX2 CPU, i.e. the ifunc picks
  __ieee754_asin_fma / __ieee754_acos_fma / __atan_fma / __ieee754_atan2_fma
  (sysdeps/x86_64/fpu/multiarch/{e_asin,s_atan,e_atan2}-fma.c, built with -mfma -mavx2, GCC default
  -ffp-contract=fast), plus the w_asin_compat/w_acos_compat wrappers (|x|>1 -> +NaN).

Required flags (informational; the lead's build.rs uses its fixed set):
  -O2 -std=gnu11 -ffp-contract=off -fno-fast-math -fno-builtin -fno-strict-aliasing -I<this dir>
  No -mfma/-march needed: every multiply-add that GCC 13.3 contracts in the glibc FMA build is an explicit
  __builtin_fma ("lp: fma" comments); EMULV/DLA_FMS in dla.h is always the fused form.
  -ffp-contract=off is REQUIRED (any further contraction changes results). Without hardware FMA,
  __builtin_fma becomes a call to the platform's fma(), which must be correctly rounded (glibc, macOS libm are).
  Assumes round-to-nearest; FP exception flags/errno are not reproduced.

How the contractions were found: gcc 13.3 -O2 -mfma -mavx2 -frounding-math -ffp-contract=fast
  -fdump-tree-widening_mul-details on the unmodified sources; the rewritten sources built with
  -ffp-contract=off -mfma -mavx2 give the same number of vfmadd/vfmsub/vfnmadd instructions
  (asin+acos 121, atan 28, atan2 47; asm differs only in scheduling/register allocation).

Smoke validation (test/smoke.c vs the VM's libm.so.6, bitwise incl. NaN bits; 1e7 inputs per
distribution: asin/acos 4e7 each, atan 4e7, atan2 6e7, plus special values / special pairs):
  gcc 13.3   fixed flags (no -mfma)      0 mismatches
  gcc 13.3   fixed flags + -mfma -mavx2  0
  clang 18   fixed flags (no -mfma)      0
  clang 18   fixed flags + -mfma         0
  (control: the unmodified sources without FMA give ~100k mismatches on 1e5 inputs, so the test discriminates)

aarch64 / macOS (UNVALIDATED, compile-only): clang --target=aarch64-apple-darwin and x86_64-apple-darwin
  compile cleanly with the fixed flags; on aarch64 every __builtin_fma is an inline fmadd/fmsub/fnmsub
  (clang folds fma(a, 2.0, c) into an add, which is exact). NaN propagation is written so that it does not
  depend on operand order (atan2's NaN branch spells out glibc's x86 result).
